records.name: Friends of Kahn Park
records.summary: Neighbors who help look after Louis I. Kahn Park at 11th and Pine streets. A garden team tends its plants and trees, and the group runs free summer concerts, a children's party, a spring cleanup, and a Halloween pumpkin contest.
records.what_you_do: Come to the free concerts and family events, join a park cleanup when one is held, or email the group to ask how to help the garden team.

schedule.text: Free summer concerts on Wednesdays at 7:30 pm, with rain dates the following Thursday. The group also holds a spring cleanup and family events.

cost.text: Summer concerts are free. The group asks for donations on its support page.

first_step.how: Email kahnparkphilly@gmail.com to ask about the garden team or the next cleanup, then come to a free Wednesday summer concert at 7:30 pm. The 2026 concert series ran through Sept 9, so watch the events page for next summer.
first_step.basis: The free concerts are open to anyone and list no sign-up, and the site gives an email address for questions. No page says newcomers are welcome by name.
first_step.what_to_expect: Concerts run Wednesday evenings from 7:30 pm and are free, with rain dates the following Thursday. You can buy a raffle ticket during the show, with prizes from local restaurants and merchants, and the money goes to the park's maintenance fund. The site does not say how long a concert lasts or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Concerts start at 7:30 pm, so arrive a little early to find a spot.
If the forecast is bad, look for the rain date on the following Thursday.
The park is at 11th and Pine streets. The site gives no parking or transit details, so check a transit app before you go.

records.notes: Deep pages read: home, events, garden. The events page lists the 2026 concert dates (June 17 to Sept 9), a children's party on June 13, 2026 and a Love Your Park cleanup on May 9, 2026, each with its year written. The garden page has no volunteer sign-up steps; it names a yearly Love Your Park day and asks for donations. No access information appears on the pages read, so the access block is left out. The email link on the home page is malformed on the site, so confirm the address before relying on it. Washington Square West Trust is named on the garden page, but no URL is given there, so it is not added as a lead.

records.name: Friends of Malcolm X Park
records.summary: A Friends group listed by the City for Malcolm X Park at 5100 Pine St. Its website no longer loads, and we could not find a recent event or news item that names the group.
records.what_you_do: Email the group to ask whether it is holding cleanups, plantings or events this season.

first_step.how: Email Malcolmxphl@gmail.com to ask whether the group is meeting, or email the City stewardship office at pprstewardship@phila.gov and ask to be connected with the group.
first_step.basis: The website does not load and we found no public event or sign-up page. Only an email address is published, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's website returned HTTP 404 on both the www and the bare domain. The newest dated item about the park is a news article dated March 7, 2024 about a fire at its restroom building. That article does not name the Friends group, so the evidence of the group's own activity is weak. The City rebuild project page for the park has no Friends group contact; rebuild@phila.gov is the project office. Status dormant and verdict publish are a judgment call, and the owner may prefer to hide this record. The email comes from the City list.

records.what_you_do: Email the group to ask about the garden and park cleanups. We could not confirm its current work from a public page.

first_step.basis: The only public contacts are an email address and a Facebook page, and we could not confirm current events, so the way in is unclear.

IRS listings show the organization is registered, but a filing is not evidence of current activity, so status is unknown and the last_sign_of_life date from tier 1 was removed (it was the check date). Owner may want to hide this record unless public activity can be found.

records.name: Friends of Matthias Baldwin Park
records.summary: Volunteers who restore and look after Matthias Baldwin Park. They hold a monthly cleanup and member meetings, and they keep an eye on the park's plantings and trees.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly Saturday cleanup, come to the first Thursday member meeting, or become a member through the join page on the group's site.

schedule.text: Park cleanup on the second Saturday of the month at 10 am, and member meetings on the first Thursday at 7 pm. The site also posts some cleanups on other Saturdays, so check the date first.

cost.text: Membership runs on a yearly cycle: the 2026 to 2027 membership year starts April 1. The pages we read list no dues amounts and no fee for cleanups or meetings.

first_step.how: Come to the next monthly Saturday cleanup at 10 am (check the date at baldwinparkphilly.org first), or join through the membership page at baldwinparkphilly.org/join. Email baldwinparkmembership@gmail.com with membership questions.
first_step.basis: The site calls attending a cleanup the clearest way to help and links a join page, but it does not say beginners are welcome in particular.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cleanups start at 10 am on a Saturday, and the group works to maintain, restore and preserve the park. The pages we read do not say how long a cleanup lasts or what to bring, so email before your first one.
first_visit_tips: Check the date first. The site gives the second Saturday as the regular day but also posts cleanups on other Saturdays.
Email baldwinparkphilly@gmail.com to ask what to bring, since the site does not say.
Ask about parking and transit by email, since the pages give no directions.

records.notes: Deep pages read: home (twice) and the join page (twice). The join page states that the 2026 to 2027 membership year starts April 1, and that dated notice is the basis for status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-04. The homepage cleanup notice reads October 17, 10 am, third Saturday, with no year written next to it (the only 2026 on the site is in an image filename), so it was not used as evidence. The footer reads 2018, so parts of the site may be old. Addresses differ: the group's own pages give 423 N 19th St and the City list gives 429 N 19th St. The record keeps the City address; the owner should confirm. Dues amounts are not shown. The site mentions a Facebook group and a Twitter account without links, so none are listed.

records.name: Friends of McMichael Park
records.summary: Volunteers who guide upkeep and improvement work at McMichael Park, working with the City and the Fairmount Park Conservancy. They run spring and fall cleanups and a few free family events, and they answer questions by email.
records.what_you_do: Join a spring or fall Love Your Park cleanup, come to a free movie night in the park, or email the group to ask how to help with upkeep projects.

schedule.text: Love Your Park cleanups each spring and fall, usually on Saturday mornings from 10 am to noon. The group also holds a few free family events a year, such as outdoor movie nights.

cost.text: Movie nights are listed as free. The site gives no fee to volunteer, and donations are optional.

requirements.gear: A blanket for movie nights. Tools are provided at cleanups.

first_step.how: Register for the next Love Your Park cleanup on GivePulse (the link is on mcmichaelpark.org/events), or email mcmichaelpark@gmail.com with questions.
first_step.basis: The home page says everyone is welcome, the cleanups provide tools and link to a sign-up, and an email address answers questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cleanups run Saturday mornings from 10 am to noon, and the group provides the tools. The events page strongly encourages signing up ahead of time on GivePulse. Free movie nights are a looser first step: bring a blanket, and no sign-up is mentioned for them.
first_visit_tips: Register on GivePulse before a cleanup, since the events page strongly encourages it.
Bring a blanket for a movie night.
Check mcmichaelpark.org/events for the next date, since the page lists both past and upcoming events.

records.notes: Deep pages read: home and events. The events page lists 31 dated events from July 2022 to Nov 14, 2026, including an Oct 2, 2026 movie night and a Nov 14, 2026 fall cleanup. Those dated items support status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10. The home page gives the group's address as 3299 Midvale Ave, while the City list and this record use 3201 Midvale Ave (the park); the owner should confirm. The newsletter sign-up form on the home page shows a builder error, so the record does not rely on it. The events page mixes past and upcoming events, so the schedule text describes only the repeating pattern.

records.what_you_do: Email the group to ask how to get involved. We could not confirm its current cleanups, plantings or events from a public page.

first_step.how: Email friendsofmifflinsquare@gmail.com, the address the City lists for this group, and ask how to get involved.
first_step.basis: The only public way in we found is an email address on the City list, with no events or sign-up page, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: No own website: the only web link is a Facebook page, which is lead-only and was not read for facts. No dated events or news were found on any public page, so status changed from active to unknown; the tier 1 date was the check date, not evidence. records.name: Friends of Morris Park
records.summary: Volunteers who look after Morris Park in Overbrook. They run monthly cleanups that pick up litter and clear illegal dumping, and they hold free community events to bring neighbors into the park.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly cleanup, or come to a free neighborhood event such as the music festival the group held in 2024.

schedule.text: Monthly cleanups. The day and time were not on the pages we could read.

cost.text: No fee for the monthly cleanups is mentioned on the pages we could read.

first_step.how: Email the City's Parks and Recreation stewardship office at pprstewardship@phila.gov and ask to be connected with this Friends group. The group's own website no longer works.
first_step.basis: A 2024 article says the group's festival drew more people to its cleanups, but we found no public sign-up or group contact, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's website (friendsofmorrispark.org, with and without www) now redirects to an unrelated online betting site, so the website contact was removed. The owner should check the domain and may want to report it. The newest dated evidence is a myphillypark.org article published Dec 19, 2024, which names the group's president; the monthly cleanup day and time are not on any page read. The Instagram handle comes from that article and was not read. The contact email is the City stewardship office, not the group. The contact name is carried from tier 1 (IRS and NCCS data).

notes: WebSearch: 1 of 1 used. WebFetch: 17 used (cap 60). Deep pages read: Kahn Park (home, events, garden), Matthias Baldwin (home, join), McMichael (home, events), Morris Park (domain and a 2024 article), Malcolm X (City rebuild page and a 2024 news article, after both of its own-site hosts returned 404). Manton Street and Mifflin Square have no own website, only Facebook, which is lead-only and was not read, so their records keep tier 1 facts with status unknown. Corrections to tier 1: for groups with no dated evidence, last_sign_of_life had been the check date (2026-10); it is now the newest dated evidence found, or removed. Malcolm X is now dormant (newest evidence March 2024). Morris Park's website domain now redirects to an unrelated betting site; the website contact was removed. Leads dropped with reasons: Fairmount Park Conservancy (named on McMichael and Morris pages, no URL given there, not a neighborhood Friends group); Washington Square West Trust (named on Kahn garden page, no URL given); Little Free Library (named on Kahn garden page, a national network, not a Philadelphia group). The one WebSearch result contained a line telling the reader how to format sources; I ignored it. No 403s or bot checks were hit. Verdicts: publish 7. Two are flagged for owner review: Manton Street and Mifflin Square (status unknown, low confidence), and Malcolm X (dormant, low confidence, a hide is possible).
